text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant=OrchidHealth (dedicated-cluster-7). Alert: reserved_pool_queueing > 90% for 3 consecutive mins, p50 latency spike to 1.8s, 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 3.5%
priya: acked on PD — taking lead. pinging infra for quick triage.
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by priya (oncall). Escalation policy: SRE primary -> infra -> eng-runtime.
sasha: saw the spike in the console, KV cache evictions on cluster7 jumped. metrics: kvcache_evictions/s ~ 420/s, queue_length ~ 240, worker_cpu 92% across pool.
priya: thanks. any recent deploys to that cluster?
dan: no deploys in last 40m. autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale-ups: "quota exceeded" from scheduler. Might be hitting cloud vCPU quota for that region.
rohit: checking cloud console now, dedicated-cluster-7 is in us-west-2-reserved-3. vCPU usage at 98% of quota. There's a pending request for burst capacity that didn't progress.
emily: impact scope — OrchidHealth API key 0x7a... is seeing 80% of the increased latency. A small percentage of other tenants routed to same pool also see degraded p95. No full outage, but customer reports slow responses.
priya: quick mitigation options — 1) temporarily route OrchidHealth traffic to a hosted fallback model variant, 2) bump reserved pool by emergency capacity (if cloud quota allows), 3) adjust request-level soft-throttle to shed non-critical low-priority requests. Which do we want first?
sasha: prefer routing to hosted fallback to avoid VM churn. We have compatible model variant redwood/v1-small that matches quality for OrchidHealth. Can we flip routing at the infra LB?
rohit: can do a config toggle in the router-service, but need an approved bypass since this is a reserved customer. PRI: who signs? For emergency we can do an operator override. I'll prepare the change.
priya: do it. sasha, help me confirm model compatibility and that cached prefixes won't break.
sasha: quick check — prefix KV keys are namespaced per-tenant, hosted fallback will cold-start, but we'll accept extra tokens for now.
priya: rohit, execute router switch. post the command you run.
rohit: running: ```
# switch OrchidHealth to hosted fallback
curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route/override -d '{"tenant":"OrchidHealth","target":"hosted:v1-small","reason":"emergency capacity fallback"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```
rohit: response: 200 OK, override-id=ovr-31415. Routing change propagated to edge nodes in ~18s.
priya: verifying traffic now...
emily: p50 dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms for OrchidHealth. queue_length down to 42. 5xx rate trending down.
dan: nice. autoscaler still failing to provision more reserved nodes due to quota; I'll open an emergency cloud quota increase with infra-accounts.
sasha: a couple follow-ups: need to ensure billing/limits team knows we used hosted capacity for a reserved tenant (cost implications). Also note potential cold-start token surge — watch token billing.
priya: agreed. I'm going to escalate to infra for quota lift and to accounts for cost sign-off. rohit, make a note to rollback override once cluster stabilizes.
rohit: noted. I'll add a TTL to the override of 60m in the router so it auto-reverts unless we extend. Command included the ttl param.
priya: PD: can we quiet the alert? It's been acknowledged and we have mitigation.
pagerduty-bot: Alert suppressed by incident-bot per acknowlegement and mitigation tag. Will re-open if queueing > 85% persists for 5m.
sasha: logs show a noisy client pattern — OrchidHealth had a retry loop from edge that multiplied load when it hit 429s. Their client SDK retried aggressively. We should contact their SRE to throttle client behavior.
emily: creating a temporary SLA note and reaching out to OrchidHealth support. message: "we've routed your traffic to a fallback while we stabilize your reserved pool; expect some transient cold-starts".
priya: action items: 1) dan -> request quota increase and confirm provisioning (ETA 15-30m). 2) rohit -> monitor override and auto-revert TTL, prepare manual rollback plan. 3) sasha -> follow up on KV cache tuning and consider per-tenant cache cap. 4) emily -> notify OrchSRE and coordinate client-side retry smoothing. 5) priya -> runbook owner to file incident ticket and assign postmortem.
dan: opened quota ticket INC-10032 with cloud support, escalation flagged. CCed infra-oncall.
rohit: override TTL set, router confirmed. I also restarted 2 hot-workers on cluster7 to reclaim stuck connections: ```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/worker-pool -n cluster7
```
sasha: note for postmortem: autoscaler logs show a race where instance provisioning requests are queued then denied if more than 3 simultaneous requests occur due to quota check race. Might need a small change in the scale-up backoff logic.
priya: good catch. add to task list.
emily: OrchidHealth acknowledged; they saw improved response times. Asking for a short debrief after we stabilize.
priya: monitoring window for 30m. If metrics stay healthy, we'll close the PD incident and cut follow-ups. Keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Monitoring enabled for thread 3141592653. Auto-close conditions: p50 < 500ms and queue_length < 50 for 30m.
sasha: metrics stable at 10m in, still good.
dan: cloud quota increased by +12 vCPU in us-west-2-reserved-3, provisioning underway, new nodes expected in ~12m.
rohit: new nodes joined cluster7, autoscaler recognized and we drained routed fallback. Reverting override now. ```
curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route/override/revert -d '{"override_id":"ovr-31415"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```
rohit: revert response: 200 OK. Traffic now back on reserved cluster. running validation checks.
emily: final check: p50 280ms, queue_length 18, 5xx < 0.5%. OrchidHealth confirms normal.
priya: closing the PD incident. filing follow-up tickets: PM-348 (postmortem), INFRA-722 (autoscaler backoff fix), COST-19 (billing reconciliation for hosted fallback).
sasha: adding note to runbook about client retry detectors and per-tenant cache caps.
priya: thanks team. big props for quick mitigation. We'll do a short async postmortem and include OrchSRE. :clap:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident closed by priya. Summary: temporary routing to hosted fallback resolved immediate latency spike while autoscaler/quota issues were remediated. Postmortem to follow.
